newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X says another lawsuit threatened.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X says another lawsuit threatened.

text.p: Bre-X Minerals Lts said on Friday it received a letter from Canadian lawyers acting for Waverly Mining Finance Plc, Montague Gold NL, Westralian Resource Projects Ltd and William P. McLucas.

Bre-X said the letter said "our clients are currently involved in investigating a number of claims against Bre-X" and certain officers which "mirror, in large part, the claims asserted by" PT Kreung Gasui.
Bre-X said it outlined PT Kreung's claims in a press release dated November 15.

The letter said "that it would be appropriate to include our clients in the meeting that is contemplated" between representatives of Bre-X and PT Kreung. Bre-X said the counsel also said if the claims are not resolved, litigation will be pursued in Alberta.
Westralian is an indirect wholly owned subsidiary of Bre-X and has not authorized any person to make claims against it.
On July 28, Bre-X said it had reached a deal with Montague to complete the transfer to Bre-X of full legal and beneficial ownership of Busang I (the Central Zone).

Under that deal, Waverly, Montague and McLucas signed a deed under which they released Bre-X, Bre-X Minerals Amsterdam BV, Westralian and their officers, directors, employees and agents from all losses or claims in connection with events which took place in 1993 and afterward in connection with the proposal for Bre-X's acquisition of an interest in Busang I.

The deed of release states, among other things: "The releases....have effect throughout the world. Accordingly, the Releasors...agree not to make any claim, demand, action or proceeding or to commence....proceedings....at any location anywhere in the world......"
The claims of this group is entirely without foundation and, in the face of the deed of release, is unsustainable, Bre-X said.

"The timing of this letter and the unsubstantiated allegations it makes are yet another example of blatant opportunism. Bre-X does not intend to be diverted from its corporate objectives by this kind of opportunism," Bre-X said in a statement.

PT Kreung has claimed up to 40 percent of the rich Busang gold property in the Indonesian province of East Kalimantan on Borneo, but Bre-X has said this partner lacks documentation to support its claims.
The partner gave Bre-X until November 22 to work out a solution. It threatened to sue Bre-X in Canadian courts if no settlement is reached.
